items.q: What two blockers does Dial name first?
items.a: **Intellectual fear** (rejection, failure, success, not enough) and a **fixed identity**. Primal fear is pain or death; most modern fear is invented. "You can't overcome something that **doesn't exist**."

items.q: If you cannot change the first thought, what can you change?
items.a: The **second thought**. Pattern: **awareness → practice → repetition** plus grace. Grocery-store judgment → name **three things you like**. Body treats imagined futures as now — if you will feel the worst, also try on the **best**.

items.q: Why does Dial treat procrastination as a why problem?
items.a: If the why is strong enough, **the how reveals itself**. Seven levels of why turned "$100k because I've never done it" into **custody and safety**. Motivation fades; **driven** people have a why that survives mood.

items.q: What fear can outweigh the unknown?
items.a: **Fear of the unchanged future** — fast-forward 5 years. Decision (*decadere*) **cuts off Plan B**. Dial's fork at 27: staying was more terrifying than leaving.

items.q: What did money and recognition fail to fill?
items.a: The **childhood void**. External search is self-search. **Rewarded workaholism** skips feeling (Maté: ask why the pain). Silence first raises anxiety, then release.

items.q: What does 'everything is your fault' actually mean?
items.a: You are the **CEO**: not that every wound was chosen, but **working through it is your responsibility**. Love the "bad" parts and they quiet; fight them and they strengthen. Asking for help is still CEO work.
